scope: Independent native-owner readback of lead-run full JS004 and Wasm004. Actual fresh native-area cases and raw/archive/source bindings checked; no new Gradle/browser/device execution by reviewer. Browser regression execution is not a finding closure or release/security/native-device certification.

native_totals.note: 50 selected functions executed on two targets; not 100 independent authored scenarios. Full project counts are290cases/19modules/48reports per target.

wasm003_failure_supplement.observation: Compose compiler required a missing Compose runtime on the IO classpath; camera/picker/io/share reached zero testcase executions.

limitations: Listener-detachment regression observes real detached iframe EventTargets synchronously, wrapping handleEvent in place and incrementing before disposed guards; negative control plus matching listener identity/capture remove checks exercise both normal/throwing disposal. It does not prove collectability/GC, broader native resource lifetime or real-page navigation cleanup.

WebView opaque-origin fixture and cookie/srcdoc tests passed in Chrome153/Linux on both Kotlin targets. Other browser engines, CSP/offline/auth/framing matrices, popup/child-window flows, trust-policy transitions and broad sandbox security remain required.

Share uses controlled navigator/clipboard Promise functions and real browser turns, not a real OS share dialog, clipboard permission or transient activation. Callback ordering/exception/ownership tests do not establish recipient consumption or file lease lifetime.

Camera's three browser cases are common request-save/restore and option-validation functions, not actual camera capture, an unsupported-launcher integration test, physical URI grants or process-death behavior.

Earlier Android Chromium history test still failed at initial readiness. No new Android host/device, iOS, AppKit, macOS JavaFX cold-start, memory profiling, native window, consumer or ABI evidence is created by these browser runs.

Generated Karma configs and selected prepared tooling/hash manifests bind observed execution context, not every installed dependency or process byte. Local root-container Chrome flags --no-sandbox/--disable-dev-shm-usage do not alter the production iframe policy or certify production security.
Inputs are hash-bound dirty working-tree diagnostics, not immutable release/consumer provenance. Keep Actions, publishing and Pages contained and all original required tests/statuses unchanged.
